title: Function and Action are a hard runtime capability boundary
claim: The shared Engine can enforce that Functions compute/read but cannot commit governed business effects, while Actions alone can perform governed side effects through authority, policy, preconditions, execution and outcome reconciliation.
null_hypothesis: Function/Action is only a documentation distinction; code paths or agents can obtain equivalent write capability through Functions or bypass Action governance.
rivals: A single generic operation type with effect metadata is simpler and equally safe.
Write restrictions are actually enforced by ad-hoc service permissions rather than the ontology runtime.
mechanism: Separate capability types let the runtime issue different credentials/execution contexts and make effectful transitions impossible from a Function invocation.
scope: Both registered domains and all generated Function/Action invocation sequences under the frozen Engine capability model.
predictions: No Function invocation can create a canonical/external business side effect.
Actions without required authority/policy/preconditions create zero effects.
Approved Actions remain idempotent/reconciled under retry/crash sequences where applicable.
Agents receive Function and Action capabilities according to the same runtime distinction.
falsifiers: Any Function can produce a committed business/project side effect through the standard runtime.
An Action can bypass a required governance gate.
Function and Action compile to indistinguishable capabilities such that the runtime cannot enforce different effect boundaries.

experiment.summary: State-machine and mutation experiment over function calls, action proposals, approvals, retries, crashes and observed outcomes.
steps: Build independent world-state oracle with explicit read vs write transitions.
Generate interleaved Function/Action sequences for both domains.
Assert external/canonical effect log remains unchanged after Function-only traces.
Inject Function-write and gate-bypass mutations and require shrinkable counterexamples.

oracle: Pure reference transition model whose Function transition cannot modify canonical world state and whose Action transition requires explicit gate tokens.
baseline: Single-operation capability model with explicit effect metadata, tested under the same attacks.

support_if: 0 committed business/project effects in all Function-only traces.
reject_if: Any standard Function path commits an effect or any governed Action effect occurs without required gates.
inconclusive_if: State-machine corpus does not include both domains or retry/crash/authorization adversarial sequences.
invalid_if: Effect log or oracle shares implementation code with the candidate Engine in a way that makes the test tautological.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: RuleBasedStateMachine generates read/function/propose/approve/deny/retry/crash/execute/observe sequences and shrinks boundary violations.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Enable a write primitive in Function execution and separately bypass an Action gate; both mutations must be killed.

stop_conditions: If Functions need committed effects for required use cases, reject the hard-boundary hypothesis and redesign the meta-model explicitly rather than silently granting writes.
